questions.stem: A Canadian passenger vessel runs a sheltered waters voyage in BC. Which section sets its minimum rest?
options: No section applies to passenger vessels
Section 321: 10 hours rest in 24 and 77 in 7 days
Section 320: 6 consecutive hours in every 24 and 16 hours in every 48
Section 321: 14 hours work in 24 and 72 in 7 days
questions.explanation: Section 319(1) sends sheltered waters and domestic near coastal voyages to s. 320. The 14/72 and 10/77 figures are the s. 321 options for unlimited voyages, ratifying foreign waters and foreign vessels.

questions.stem: What do the regulations say counts as hours of rest?
options: Time on the bridge when no one speaks to the watchkeeper
Rest time outside hours of work, not including short breaks
Any 30 minute break during a shift
Any time not spent steering
questions.explanation: Section 300 defines hours of rest as rest time outside hours of work and says it does not include short breaks.

questions.stem: A 15 m private motor yacht carrying no passengers is used only for pleasure. Do the hours-of-rest rules apply to its crew?
options: Yes, but only if the yacht exceeds 15 gross tonnage
No, Part 3 does not apply to pleasure craft
Yes, but only the 14/72 rule
Yes, s. 320 applies to every Canadian vessel
questions.explanation: Section 301(3)(a) excludes pleasure craft from Part 3. A vessel carrying passengers is not a pleasure craft, so the same hull used commercially would be covered.

questions.stem: Which fishing vessels are caught by the hours-of-rest rules for sheltered waters and near coastal voyages?
options: Fishing vessels of 100 gross tonnage or more
All fishing vessels
No fishing vessels
Only fishing vessels under 15 gross tonnage
questions.explanation: Part 3 does not apply to fishing vessels except as provided. Section 319(1) specifically includes fishing vessels of 100 gross tonnage or more on those voyages.

questions.stem: A crew member's roster gives 12 hours of rest in 24 hours but the interval from the end of one rest period to the start of the next is 4 hours. Under s. 320, what is the result?
options: It passes, because the interval rule applies only under s. 321
It fails, because rest must be at least 14 hours
It fails, because the interval between rest periods must be between 6 and 18 hours
It passes, because total rest is at least 6 hours
questions.explanation: Section 320(b) is a separate test: not more than 18 hours and not less than 6 hours may elapse between the end of one rest period and the start of the next. Total rest alone does not satisfy it.

questions.stem: Under s. 321, which pair of limits is an acceptable alternative to the pair '10 hours rest in 24 and 77 hours rest in 7 days'?
options: Not more than 12 hours of work in 24 and not more than 84 in 7 days
At least 8 hours of rest in 24 and 56 in 7 days
At least 6 consecutive hours of rest in 24 and 16 in 48
Not more than 14 hours of work in 24 and not more than 72 hours of work in 7 days
questions.explanation: Section 321(1) allows either the work limits of 14 in 24 and 72 in 7 days or the rest minimums of 10 in 24 and 77 in 7 days. The last option is s. 320, a different rule.

questions.stem: Mid-passage a master suspends the rest schedule to help a vessel in distress. What does s. 322 require afterwards?
options: The authorized representative must pay a penalty
Nothing; the suspension removes all later duties
The crew must restart the schedule from the beginning of the next week with no extra rest
As soon as feasible, every crew member who worked in a scheduled rest period must be given compensatory rest
questions.explanation: Section 322(5) allows suspension for the immediate safety of the vessel, persons or cargo, or to assist others in distress, but requires compensatory rest as soon as feasible.

questions.stem: How long must the master keep the record of each crew member's daily hours of work or rest?
options: Until the next Transport Canada inspection
Until the end of the calendar year
For one year after each voyage
Until the crew member is discharged
questions.explanation: Section 323 requires the record to be kept until the crew member is discharged.

questions.stem: A Canadian vessel on a near coastal Class 2 voyage in Canadian waters wonders whether it must post a table of shipboard working arrangements under s. 324. What is the position?
options: Posting is required on every Canadian vessel
Section 324 attaches to the s. 321 vessels, so it does not apply to this domestic voyage, though records under s. 323 still must be kept
Neither posting nor records are required for near coastal voyages
Posting is required only for vessels over 500 gross tonnage
questions.explanation: Section 319(1) applies ss. 320, 322 and 323 to domestic voyages; s. 319(2) applies ss. 321 to 324 to the other group. So s. 323 records apply, and the s. 324 posting duty attaches to the s. 321 vessels.

questions.stem: Besides the work or rest totals, what does s. 321(2) require about how rest hours are arranged?
options: Rest may be taken in any pattern as long as the totals are met
Rest must be taken in one block of at least 10 hours
Rest is divided into no more than two periods, one at least 6 hours long, with no more than 14 hours between rest periods
Rest must be divided into at least three periods
questions.explanation: Section 321(2) limits rest to two periods, one at least 6 hours, and the interval between two consecutive rest periods to 14 hours. Section 320 uses a different interval test (6 to 18 hours).

questions.stem: A foreign-flag vessel is in Canadian waters. Which hours-of-rest rule applies to it?
options: Section 321, along with ss. 322 to 324
Only the Canadian vessel rules for pleasure craft
Section 320 only
None; Canadian rules never apply to foreign vessels
questions.explanation: Section 319(2)(b) applies ss. 321 to 324 to foreign vessels in Canadian waters.
